# Lab 3 - published checks (Tier A)

These are the checks `itsmlab verify 3` runs; the grader runs the same checker on the receipted commit,
with your login's kb-index profile, on its own machine. Bundles: **Core** is pass/fail as a whole (every
Core spec must pass), **Stretch** passes at any two of three, and `slo.md`'s prose and `ai-first-draft.md`
are read by the lecturer. Ids are stable; every rule id (`M-nn`) is defined in `MONITORING-SPEC.md`.

Every number is measured by the checker's own instruments: its load generator (oha 1.16.0), its own
Prometheus 3.15.0 scraping your service and evaluating your rules, and promtool. Your own Prometheus and
Grafana are never started by the checker.

A request that only prepares a check is not a check: when one fails, every check that depends on it is
reported as `error` with the reason. Limits: the build is untimed in Tier A and killed after 300 s in
Tier B; `docker compose up --wait svcdesk kb-index` and the health checks have 120 s together; the
measurement takes about 100 s.

## L3-CORE-1 `compose-up` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L3-CORE-1.01 | compose file defines service svcdesk with build | a compose file at the repo root (discovery as in Lab 1) defines a service `svcdesk` with a `build:` key |
| L3-CORE-1.02 | no host-path bind mounts on svcdesk or kb-index | in the resolved configuration neither `svcdesk` nor `kb-index` has a host-path bind mount (your own Prometheus and Grafana may bind-mount their configuration: the checker never starts them) |
| L3-CORE-1.03 | a kb-index service runs the course image | a service `kb-index` with `image: ghcr.io/swasik/seeded-toxic:<tag>`; the checker replaces image and login with its own, so what matters is that your stack has it |
| L3-CORE-1.04 | compose up --wait svcdesk kb-index within 120 s | after an untimed `docker compose build`, `docker compose up --wait svcdesk kb-index` succeeds within 120 s |
| L3-CORE-1.05 | GET /health answers 200, kb-index answers /healthz | `GET /health` on svcdesk answers 200 within the same 120 s, and `kb-index` answers `GET /healthz` |

## L3-CORE-2 `kb-search-metrics` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L3-CORE-2.01 | GET /kb/search passes the upstream hits through | `GET /kb/search?q=vpn%20drops` answers 200 JSON whose `query` echoes q and whose `hits` equal kb-index's own answer for the same q (repeated, at most 3 times, while it comes back 502) |
| L3-CORE-2.02 | a bad q is refused | no `q`, and a 201-character `q`: 400 or 422 with a top-level `error` object |
| L3-CORE-2.03 | an upstream failure is a 502 | `q=force-error-itsmlab` (kb-index answers 503): 502 with `error.code` `upstream_unavailable` |
| L3-CORE-2.04 | /metrics exposes the request histogram | `GET /metrics` (text format) declares `http_server_request_duration_seconds` as a histogram and exposes its `_bucket`, `_sum` and `_count` |
| L3-CORE-2.05 | the histogram's labels are the three of M-04 | every series of the histogram has exactly the labels `http_request_method`, `http_route`, `http_response_status_code` (plus `le` on buckets) |
| L3-CORE-2.06 | the checker's requests are observed on /kb/search | the requests of 2.01-2.03 appear under `http_route="/kb/search"` with the status codes they got |
| L3-CORE-2.07 | routes are templates, never raw paths | no label value contains the checker's random ids or query strings, and `GET /tickets/<id>` is observed on a route template |
| L3-CORE-2.08 | one ladder, at most 30 boundaries, seconds | every label set has the same finite `le` boundaries, at most 30 of them; the `_sum` increment of one `/kb/search` request is below 10 (seconds, not milliseconds) |
| L3-CORE-2.09 | the cardinality probe grows the series by at most 5 | after a warm-up request of each kind, 250 `GET /itsmlab-probe/<uuid>`, 250 `GET /tickets/<uuid>` and 500 `GET /health?itsmlab-probe=<uuid>` add at most 5 series to `/metrics` |

## L3-CORE-3 `buckets` (core)

| id | check | expected |
|---|---|---|
| L3-CORE-3.01 | the measurement completed | the M-08 run (60 s open-loop at 40 requests/s, latency-corrected, 64 connections) got answers to at least 95 % of the scheduled requests, with transport errors below 1 % |
| L3-CORE-3.02 | no bypass: q is at least 0.9 x q_kb | the p99 of `/kb/search` (q) is at least 0.9 times the p99 of kb-index measured directly (q_kb) |
| L3-CORE-3.03 | one upstream call per request | kb-index's `/stats` request counter rose, over the M-08 run, by the number of responses oha received within 2 % |
| L3-CORE-3.04 | every response observed once | the `_count` increment of the `/kb/search` series over the run equals the responses within 2 % |
| L3-CORE-3.05 | your ladder resolves q | the bucket (lo, hi] of your ladder that contains q has hi - lo at most 0.20 x q |
| L3-CORE-3.06 | the histogram's own p99 agrees with q | `histogram_quantile(0.99)` over the run's bucket increments (Prometheus's interpolation) is within 25 % of q |
| L3-CORE-3.07 | ai-first-draft.md is complete and consistent | front matter `lab3_first_draft` as the template shows (the `lab3_flawed_ladder` block is 3.09's); the evidence's bucket and relative width follow from the declared ladder and p99; your p99 is within 30 % of q; with `source: ai`, `## Prompt` and `## Answer` hold the exchange verbatim |
| L3-CORE-3.08 | the first draft's verdict agrees with the measurement | M-11 applied to the draft's ladder at 0.95q, q and 1.05q: a clear result must match the verdict (`confirmed` = resolves); a result too close to call accepts either |
| L3-CORE-3.09 | the flawed ladder is refuted with its arithmetic | `lab3_flawed_ladder.verdict` is `refuted`, and its evidence is consistent with the shipped ladder and uses your draft's p99 (to 1 %) |
